In some cases, HMD may cause only mild vision problems that can be managed with corrective lenses or low vision aids. However, as the disease progresses, it can lead to significant vision loss and even legal blindness in some cases.

While HMD can cause significant visual impairment, it does not typically result in complete blindness as other parts of the retina outside the macula are still functional, allowing for peripheral vision. However, it is important to note that the impact of HMD on a person's vision can be unpredictable and dependent on individual factors. 

If you have concerns about HMD or any other vision problems, it is recommended to consult an eye doctor or ophthalmologist for a proper diagnosis and treatment plan.

Based on the picture you have attached, it does seem like the scar is red and raised, which indicates that it is still in the early stages of healing. It is normal to feel depressed and frustrated about the scar revision, but it is important to stay positive and patient. Scar healing is a slow process, and it can take weeks or even months for the scar to fully heal and fade. In the meantime, try to avoid harsh sunlight, smoking and environmental pollutants, as they can all have a negative impact on scar healing.

Wishing you a speedy recovery.

input: Hi doctor,I had unprotected sex on day 13 of my cycle and had an I-pill a day later. Again, I had sex in a gap of three days after the intake of tablet. I am really worried if I should take the pill again. This was a terrible mistake. Please help.

So, it is an unsafe period to have sex. And, if you have once unprotected sex and have taken I-pill (emergency contraceptive pill) once, then why to make mistake for the second time. Because, I-pill in itself is not 100% effective even if taken once. There is no study about two times taken I-pill. It works with two mechanisms. First of all, it will delay ovulation and second, it brings bleeding. So, if pregnancy happens, it resists implantation. In your case, if I believe that ovulation is delayed while you have taken the tablet, then it is good. If you have taken the tablet for the second time, then the ovulation is more delayed and period will be somewhat late with more chance of avoiding pregnancy. The second thing is that with I-pill your period cycle can become irregular. The chance of that increases more if you have taken two times. Because, it is a chemical (hormone), which is produced in your body to maintain your regular cycle. And, when you take it from outside it can disturb your normal cycle. If you do not want pregnancy in the first place, then either use condom or other method as preferred by you both after discussing with your doctor. I-pill is an emergency contraceptive and not a regular contraceptive pill that you can take as and when required. It should be taken when fear of failure of normal contraception is more. input: Hello doctor,I am a 29-year-old female. I was just diagnosed with chronic urticaria. I went to an allergic specialist for skin testing because my skin was so sensitive I reacted to everything. They then did the RAST test on me. Everything came out class 0 except for egg white, wheat, and oats being class 2 and milk, and hazelnut being class 1. Can these cause anaphylaxis? How accurate are the RAST test? I was put on an elimination diet but the hives are still there. I occasionally get angioedema with it also. Can angiodema cause anaphylaxis? As you can see I am so scared for my throat to close up that I am scared to eat anything. I have only been eating a couple of things daily and live off that.
answer_icliniq: Hello,  Welcome to ChatDoctor. RAST is a highly accurate test. If the test is positive for a specific allergen, it shows that you are sensitized to that particular allergen. This means that you may mount an allergic response when you are exposed to that allergen. However, it does not mean that you will necessarily have an allergic reaction to that substance and, nor does it mean that any reactions will be severe. If the test is negative, it means that one does not have the ability to mount an allergic reaction to that allergen and any symptoms one may be experiencing are probably not due to an allergic reaction to that substance. However, the results of the RAST need to be interpreted in conjunction with your clinical history. e.g the presence of allergy to some or few allergens which may possibly be present either in the environment or food does not necessarily mean that they are responsible for the symptoms because if they are not even present in the environment or food of an individual, then they are irrelevant. In your case, an elimination diet has not helped thus proving the fact that RAST test results should be carefully interpreted along with clinical history and does not necessarily mean that you will necessarily have an allergic reaction to the substance that you tested. Angioedema is frequently associated with urticaria. Pathogenesis is the same for both urticaria as well as angioedema. The presence of angioedema does not always mean that it is a part of anaphylaxis. Angioedema can be a part of anaphylaxis in those individuals who have a severe allergic reaction to an allergen with high levels of antibodies circulating in the blood. Since you have only class 1 and 2 level antibodies therefore it is unlike that these antigens or allergens would cause anaphylaxis.

Firstly, the RAST test is generally considered to be a reliable test for detecting IgE-mediated allergies. It measures the amount of IgE antibodies in your blood to specific allergens. However, it isn't 100% accurate and can still give false positive or false negative results. So, it's not uncommon to have positive RAST test results but not have any symptoms upon exposure to the allergens.

Regarding the potential for anaphylaxis, a positive RAST test doesn't necessarily mean that you will experience anaphylaxis upon exposure to a particular allergen. Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that can affect multiple organs in the body, including the airways, cardiovascular system, and skin. Not everyone who has a positive allergy test will experience anaphylaxis. However, it is possible to have an anaphylactic reaction to any allergen, not just the ones you tested positive for.

Angioedema is a condition in which there is a rapid swelling of the deeper layers of the skin and tissue beneath. It can occur in response to an allergic reaction, but it can also be caused by other factors, such as certain medications or underlying medical conditions. While angioedema isn't typically associated with anaphylaxis, it can cause swelling in the throat, which can potentially lead to difficulty breathing.

It's understandable to be afraid of eating due to the possibility of an allergic reaction. However, it's important to have a well-balanced and varied diet to ensure that your body is getting all the nutrients it needs to function properly. You may want to consider working with a registered dietitian or nutritionist who can help you develop a safe and balanced meal plan that takes your food allergies into account.

I hope this helps. If you have any further concerns, I encourage you to speak with your doctor or allergist.

Contoura LASIK, on the other hand, is a type of custom LASIK procedure that uses topography-guided laser technology. This technology can provide better outcomes for patients with highly irregular corneas, such as those with keratoconus.

If the tooth is vital, he will put some medication over the pulp to let it heal and then fill with the pulp friendly restoration. However, if the tooth is dead, I would suggest you to go for the root canal treatment (after evaluating the condition of the tooth and soft tissue). Meanwhile, keep your oral hygiene good, brush twice daily and floss regularly. Use mouth rinses to clean the mouth after meals.

The two types of bleeding that can occur during a stroke are intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH).

ICH occurs when blood vessels within the brain rupture and blood leaks into the surrounding brain tissue. This type of bleeding is typically considered more dangerous because it can lead to significant damage to the surrounding brain tissue and can be life-threatening.

SAH occurs when blood vessels in the brain’s surface or within the subarachnoid space (the area between the brain and the tissues that cover it) rupture and blood leaks into this space. While SAH can also be serious and may require surgery, it is generally considered less severe than ICH.

The reason why ICH is considered more dangerous is due to the amount of blood and pressure that builds up within the brain from the bleeding. This can cause significant damage to the brain tissue and increase the risk of complications such as seizures, brain swelling, and coma.

It is important to seek medical attention immediately if you suspect you have had a stroke, so that the type and severity of the stroke can be determined and appropriate treatment can begin quickly.

Based on your blood work, it appears that your iron levels are improving with supplementation. However, it is important to note that iron supplementation can have side effects, including gastrointestinal upset, constipation, and nausea. In rare cases, iron supplementation can lead to iron toxicity, which can cause symptoms like abdominal pain, vomiting, and liver damage.

To monitor for iron toxicity, it is important to have regular blood work done while taking iron supplements. In general, it is recommended to have blood work done every 3-6 months while taking iron supplements.

Regarding the duration and dosage of iron supplementation, it is best to follow the advice of your healthcare provider. Depending on your individual situation, they may recommend continuing iron supplementation until your ferritin levels are in the normal range, or they may suggest discontinuing supplementation and rechecking levels in a few months.

I hope this information is helpful to you. If you have any further questions or concerns, please consult with your healthcare provider.

Implantation bleeding typically occurs 6-12 days after fertilization and a few days before your expected period. It occurs when the fertilized egg implants itself in the uterine lining. If you experience spotting or light bleeding after your period, it is unlikely to be implantation bleeding, but it could be breakthrough bleeding or irregular bleeding.

While it is possible for fertilization to occur a week before your period, the chances are lower compared to the days around ovulation. The fertile window is typically considered to be the 5 days leading up to ovulation and the day of ovulation itself.

If you'd like to add an extra layer of protection to the condom, starting a hormonal birth control pill (also known as oral contraceptives) could be a good option.

There are a few different types of hormonal birth control pills available, but combined oral contraceptives (COCs) are the most commonly prescribed. COCs contain both estrogen and progestin hormones, and work by preventing ovulation (the release of an egg from your ovaries), thickening cervical mucus (which makes it harder for sperm to swim up into the uterus), and thinning the lining of the uterus (so that if any sperm do get past the cervical mucus, they have a harder time implanting in the uterus).

To avoid disrupting your regular menstrual cycle, it's important to start the pills at the right time. If you have a 28-day cycle and your last period started 7 days ago, your next period should be due in about 21 days. If you start the pills now, you can expect to have some irregular bleeding in the first month or two (this is called "breakthrough bleeding" and is normal), but your next period should come on schedule. Just keep taking the pills at the same time every day, and be sure to use the condom at the same time.

Keep in mind that hormonal birth control pills aren't 100% effective, even when used perfectly - they're about 99% effective with perfect use (meaning taking the pill at the same time every day, without missing any doses), and about 91% effective with typical use (meaning missing a pill or taking it at a different time than usual). Using a condom along with the pill can help reduce that risk even further.

Talk to a healthcare professional to determine which type of COC is right for you. They can help you choose the appropriate one based on your medical history and other factors. I hope this helps!

Hello! The decision of what type of anesthesia to use depends on the type of procedure being performed and the patient's medical history. 

Twilight anesthesia, also known as conscious sedation, is a light form of anesthesia where the patient is sedated but still conscious and able to respond to verbal commands. It is commonly used in minor procedures and does not require intubation or ventilation. 

Nerve block anesthesia is a local anesthesia that involves injecting a medication around a nerve or group of nerves to numb the area where the procedure will be performed. This type of anesthesia allows the patient to remain awake and aware during the procedure, but without any pain. 

General anesthesia involves the administration of medication that causes the patient to become unconscious and unaware of the operation. This type of anesthesia is typically used for more invasive or longer procedures.

When it comes to anxiety and nervousness, it is important to understand that both anesthesia options can be tailored to the patient's needs. Patients who are more anxious may benefit from a combination of both nerve block anesthesia and twilight anesthesia to help them relax before the procedure. 

It's best to speak with your treating physician about the type of procedure being performed, your medical history, and any concerns you may have to determine the best anesthesia option for you.

The best to halt progression is corneal collagen cross-linking (C3R). This procedure causes the development of a lot of chemical bonds inside your cornea stabilizing it, thus preventing it from bulging out further. This procedure can only bring stabilization and will not improve your vision. For vision, we have a number of surgeries and implants, which can improve vision after corneal collagen cross-linking. answer_chatgpt:
The treatment options for advanced keratoconus include corneal collagen cross-linking, corneal transplant surgery, and implantable collamer lenses. The choice of treatment depends on the severity of the condition and the individual patient's needs.

Corneal collagen cross-linking is a procedure that uses UV-A light and a photosensitizing agent to stiffen the cornea and prevent further bulging. This treatment can slow or stop the progression of keratoconus but may not improve vision significantly.

Corneal transplant surgery involves replacing the damaged cornea with a healthy donor cornea. This procedure is typically reserved for advanced keratoconus cases where vision cannot be corrected with other treatments.

Implantable collamer lenses are placed inside the eye and provide continuous vision correction without the need for glasses or contact lenses. This treatment may be an option for patients who cannot undergo corneal transplant surgery.

It is possible that with successful treatment, you may not need to use lenses in the future. However, every patient's case is unique, and it is important to discuss your options with your ophthalmologist or corneal specialist.

PVCs usually do not cause any serious problems and can be brought on by stress, anxiety, caffeine, alcohol, and certain medications.

The severity of the condition varies depending on whether the individual inherits one or two abnormal beta globin genes. Beta thalassemia trait means that the individual has one abnormal beta globin gene and one normal beta globin gene. It is usually not associated with any significant health problems.

If you have no family history of beta thalassemia, and you are not a carrier, then your children will not inherit beta thalassemia. However, if the child inherited the abnormal gene from the father, then the child will be a carrier like the father. Generally, people with beta thalassemia trait don't need treatment and lead normal lives. But if both parents have beta thalassemia trait, there is a risk of having a child with beta thalassemia major, which is a severe form of the condition.

input: Hello doctor,I had two sexual encounters with women whom I do not know their HIV status. Both were vaginal and a condom was worn. In the fourth and fifth weeks, I had a fourth-generation antibody-antigen test performed and it came back negative. Should I be retested again?
answer_icliniq: Hello,  Welcome to ChatDoctor. It is a good idea to get repeat testing, here is why. The antibody testing at the fourth and fifth weeks can give you some idea of the HIV (human immuno deficiency virus) status, but the one at 12 weeks after the exposure will confirm the negative status completely. The reason being the window period. The window period is a duration where a person can have HIV but still test HIV negative. The fourth generation is antigen-antibody based testing and the best we have so far for screening. When suspected acute HIV infection or high risk exposure, PCR (polymerase chain reaction) is the best in the fourth and fifth weeks post-exposure. Of note, the window period for a fourth-generation antigen-antibody test is short as compared to other HIV tests available (about four weeks). Usually by this time, 95% of infection will be detected in the blood. In general, there is a three month window period for HIV after a given exposure, and therefore for the fouth generation testing to confirm that a person is more than 99.9% infectious. Hence the 12 weeks retesting is recommended. I hope this helps.

Hello! It's normal to hear some sound when you're in a quiet room, even if your hearing is perfectly fine. This is called subjective tinnitus, which is the perception of sound without any external source. It can be caused by a number of things, including stress, exposure to loud noises, and even certain medications. It's possible that your father's explanation of wax build-up causing the sound is only partially correct. While wax build-up can certainly cause hearing issues, it's unlikely that it would cause constant, low-grade tinnitus.

The sound you're hearing may be the result of blood flow, which is completely normal. In fact, many people hear a soft rushing sound when they put their ear up to a pillow or take a shower. This is due to the blood flow in your head.

However, if you're hearing a persistent, bothersome sound that is interfering with your daily life, it's probably a good idea to see an ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialist. A specialist may be able to determine the exact cause of the sound and recommend appropriate treatment if necessary.

The surgical procedure most commonly used for fetal hydronephrosis is called pyeloplasty. This surgery involves repairing the blockage in the renal pelvis by reattaching the ureter to the renal pelvis.

The outlook for surgery depends on the severity of the blockage and the success of the surgery. In most cases, surgery is successful and the kidneys function normally after the procedure. However, in some cases, the kidneys may continue to have some degree of damage, which can lead to long-term kidney problems.

It is important to note that fetal hydronephrosis itself is not a life-threatening condition. However, if left untreated, it can lead to kidney damage and other complications.

Hello. A pacemaker (PM) is a device that is implanted under the skin, typically in the upper chest, to regulate the heartbeat. It is often used to treat bradycardia (a slow heartbeat), which can occur as a result of certain heart conditions or as a side effect of medication. The pacemaker senses the heart’s electrical activity and responds by sending an electrical impulse to the heart to keep it beating at a steady rate.

In some cases, a pacemaker can also be used to treat certain types of arrhythmias, or abnormal heart rhythms. For example, if you have episodes of bradycardia, along with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF), a pacemaker can help to regulate your heart rate during normal sinus rhythm (when your heart is beating normally), and also provide a backup in case your heart rate becomes too slow during an episode of PAF.

During an episode of atrial fibrillation, the pacemaker is typically inactive because the electrical impulses that trigger the heartbeat are coming from multiple sources in the heart, rather than from the pacemaker. However, the pacemaker can still play an important role in managing your heart rhythm overall.

In your case, if your cardiologist has recommended a pacemaker, it may be because your episodes of bradycardia are becoming more frequent, which could put you at risk for complications like dizziness, fainting, or even heart failure. A pacemaker can help to regulate your heart rate and prevent these complications.

It's important to discuss any concerns or questions you have with your cardiologist, as they can provide you with more specific information about how a pacemaker may help you manage your atrial fibrillation and other heart conditions.

It also means that if you do become pregnant, the baby will not develop properly in the first months of its life. The best way to correct this problem is to have surgery to remove the wall between the two sides of your uterus and reconnect the two sides. This is called a hysterosalpingogram (HSG). You should discuss this operation with your gynecologist.

Hello! LASIK surgery is a popular and effective method of correcting vision problems such as myopia (nearsightedness), hyperopia (farsightedness), and astigmatism. Customized LASIK and bladeless LASIK are two different techniques used to perform this procedure. 

Customized LASIK, also known as Wavefront-guided LASIK, uses advanced computer technology to create a 3D map of your eye. This map is used to guide the laser during the procedure, resulting in a more personalized and precise treatment. This technique is often recommended for patients with unique visual aberrations such as higher-order aberrations.

Bladeless LASIK, also known as Femtosecond LASIK, uses a specialized laser to create a corneal flap instead of using a blade. The laser creates microscopic bubbles within the cornea, which allows for a more precise and consistent corneal flap creation. This technique is generally considered to be safer and more precise than traditional LASIK, which uses a blade to create the corneal flap.

It is important to discuss these options with your LASIK surgeon to determine which technique is best for you based on your specific individual needs and visual aberrations. They can conduct a thorough eye exam and provide guidance on the best course of action for your eyes.

Liver hemangiomas are benign tumors that occur in the liver. They are usually asymptomatic and detected incidentally during an imaging test, such as an ultrasound or MRI scan. Hemangiomas are the most common benign liver tumor and are estimated to occur in up to 7% of the population. 

Liver hemangiomas can vary in size and appearance on imaging tests. In general, larger hemangiomas tend to be easier to diagnose because they have a characteristic appearance. However, smaller hemangiomas may present as non-specific liver lesions that are difficult to distinguish from other liver tumors, such as metastases. 

Ultrasound is a non-invasive imaging test that uses sound waves to produce images of the organs in the body. It is a good first-line test for detecting liver lesions, but it has limited sensitivity and specificity for distinguishing between different types of liver tumors. MRI is a more sensitive imaging test that can help to better characterize liver lesions, but it is more expensive and involves the use of a contrast agent.

Based on the description in your report, it sounds like your liver lesions are likely benign hemangiomas. Hyperechogenicity is a characteristic finding of liver hemangiomas on ultrasound, and it is a sign of increased reflectivity of the sound waves by a mass relative to the surrounding liver tissue. In addition, the fact that the lesions were not seen on the previous CT scan is consistent with a diagnosis of liver hemangioma, which can be missed on CT scans without contrast.

In conclusion, it is possible that your liver lesions are benign hemangiomas, which are common and usually do not require any treatment. However, it is important to follow up with your healthcare provider and to have any necessary follow-up tests to confirm the diagnosis and monitor the size of the lesions over time. MRI may be recommended for further evaluation, but it is important to discuss any concerns or questions you have with your healthcare provider.

This suggests that your diabetes may not be well-controlled and you may need to adjust your medication and lifestyle habits to improve your blood sugar levels.

The urine microalbumin to creatinine ratio is a test that measures the amount of albumin, a type of protein, in your urine. When the kidneys are working well, they filter out excess albumin so that it doesn't end up in the urine. However, when the kidneys are damaged, albumin can leak into the urine. A ratio of 116 suggests that your kidneys may be experiencing some damage due to diabetes.

It's important to speak with your doctor about these test results and work on managing your diabetes and protecting your kidney health. This may involve making changes to your diet and exercise habits, adjusting your medication regimen, and monitoring your blood glucose and kidney function over time.

Thoracic, thoracolumbar, and lumbar fusions are different types of spinal fusion surgeries that involve the thoracic (upper back), thoracolumbar (middle back), and lumbar (lower back) regions of the spine. 

Thoracic fusion involves fusing one or more vertebrae in the upper back region, while lumbar fusion involves fusing one or more vertebrae in the lower back region. Thoracolumbar fusion involves fusing the thoracic and lumbar regions together, typically to treat a deformity or injury that spans both regions.

The spinal canal is not reduced in size as it would be during a thoracic fusion.

It is usually an asymptomatic, benign condition, and does not require any specific treatment. It means that the electrical signal from the upper chamber of the heart (atria) is delayed slightly as it passes through the AV node before it reaches the lower chamber of the heart (ventricles).

The cause of first-degree AV block can vary and may be present in normal individuals without any underlying heart disease. However, it can also occur as a result of certain medications, electrolyte imbalances, metabolic disorders or structural heart issues. If there is an underlying heart disease, like coronary artery disease, hypertension, or myocarditis, it may need to be addressed.

Therefore, if there are any underlying symptoms, medical conditions or abnormalities found during physical examination, additional tests or investigations may be needed to determine the cause of the first-degree AV block. In general, treatment is not required for first-degree AV block, but it is important to monitor any symptoms, and the condition should be followed up with regular appointments with your healthcare provider.

Hi there! Yes, there are certain EKG findings that suggest bifascicular block. Bifascicular block refers to the presence of conduction block in two of the three main conduction pathways in the heart. Specifically, it refers to the combination of right bundle branch block (RBBB) and either left anterior fascicular block (LAFB) or left posterior fascicular block (LPFB). 

Some common EKG findings associated with bifascicular block include a widened QRS complex (>120 ms) due to RBBB, as well as abnormal axis deviation due to the LAFB or LPFB. 

If the bifascicular block is due to LAFB, the QRS axis may be shifted to the right (i.e. a positively deflected QRS complex in lead II and a negatively deflected QRS complex in lead aVF). On the other hand, if the bifascicular block is due to LPFB, the QRS axis may be shifted to the left (i.e. a negatively deflected QRS complex in lead II and a positively deflected QRS complex in lead aVF). 

It's worth noting that bifascicular block can be a tricky diagnosis to make, as other conditions can produce similar EKG findings. In some cases, additional testing such as cardiac imaging or electrophysiological studies may be needed to confirm the diagnosis. 

However, as a general rule, if you see a widened QRS complex with abnormal axis deviation, particularly if it's associated with symptoms such as fainting or palpitations, it's important to consider the possibility of bifascicular block and involve a cardiologist in the evaluation. 

I hope this helps, and good luck with your EKG studies!

Your father's cardiologist and surgeon will consider factors such as age, overall health, and the severity of the heart disease. The two types of valves commonly used are the mechanical and the biological valves. The options could be a medical abortion (abortion with medicines) or a surgical abortion (abortion with surgery).

answer_chatdoctor: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) are both enzymes that are found in the prostate gland. PSA is produced by the epithelial cells of the prostate gland and is released into the bloodstream. It can be detected in the blood as early as five years before any clinical signs of prostate cancer appear. PAP is produced by the smooth muscle cells of the prostate gland and is released into the semen. Elevated levels of PAP may indicate inflammation or obstruction of the prostate ducts. It is not a routine test but is sometimes used to monitor patients with prostate problems such as benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

answer_chatgpt:
Dear patient,

Escitalopram and Buspirone are very different types of medications that are used to treat anxiety disorders.

Escitalopram belongs to a class of medications called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). It works by increasing the levels of the neurotransmitter serotonin in the brain, which helps to improve mood and reduce anxiety. Escitalopram is commonly used to treat generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), as well as major depression and panic disorder.

Buspirone, on the other hand, belongs to a class of medications called anxiolytics. It works by binding to serotonin and dopamine receptors in the brain, which helps to reduce anxiety and improve mood. Buspirone is not a benzodiazepine and does not have the same potential for abuse or dependence as benzodiazepine medications, which are commonly used to treat anxiety disorders.

The main difference between these medications is how they work in the brain. Escitalopram primarily affects the levels of serotonin in the brain, while Buspirone affects both serotonin and dopamine receptors. Buspirone is usually considered a second-line treatment for anxiety disorders, while SSRIs like escitalopram are considered first-line treatments.

It is important to note that everyone responds differently to medications and there are many factors that can influence which medication is best for an individual. Therefore, it is important to talk to your doctor about your symptoms and any concerns you may have, and together you can decide which medication is best for you.

Based on the history provided, it seems like your wife is experiencing some cardiac symptoms. The TMT (Treadmill Test) is a screening test to evaluate the presence of any underlying heart disease. A positive TMT indicates that there might be a blockage in your wife's coronary arteries, which can further cause chest pain, shortness of breath, or syncope (fainting). 

Angiography and Stress Echocardiogram are diagnostic procedures performed to evaluate the severity and location of the blockage. Angiography is an invasive test that involves inserting a catheter through a blood vessel in the arm or groin and advancing it to the heart to inject contrast media to take X-ray images. On the other hand, Stress Echocardiography is a non-invasive test where the heart's ultrasound images are captured before, during, and after exercise or the injection of medication called dobutamine. 

Both procedures are useful in detecting coronary artery disease, but the decision about which test to perform first depends on the person's medical condition, symptoms, and overall health. A stress echocardiogram is a good option if your wife is not a good candidate for angiography or if the physician is unsure about the significance of positive TMT. However, if your wife has high-risk symptoms or is at high risk of heart disease, angiography may be appropriate.

Based on your wife's age and the symptoms of palpitations, I would recommend that she continue to undergo further evaluation and management under the guidance of a cardiologist. It is vital to take timely steps to prevent any complications and promote heart health.

Regarding the choice between autograft and allograft, there are pros and cons to both options. 

Autografts are taken from your own body, usually from the hamstring or patellar tendon. The benefit is that there is no risk of disease transmission, and the chance of rejection is greatly reduced. Autografts also offer better incorporation, and are typically stronger and more durable than allografts. However, a disadvantage of autografts is the possibility of donor site morbidity, such as discomfort or weakness in the area where the graft was taken from. 

Allografts, on the other hand, are taken from a cadaver and can be used for a variety of purposes, including AC joint reconstruction. Allografts eliminate the need to harvest tissue from the patient, and can provide a larger graft than autograft options. However, there is a slightly higher risk of disease transmission with allografts compared to autografts. 

Ultimately, the decision on which graft to use will be up to you and your surgeon. Factors to consider may include the specifics of your injury, your age, and your overall health. It's important to have an open and frank discussion with your surgeon about the pros and cons of each option and the risks and benefits of each.

Firstly, let me explain what a nuchal translucency (NT) scan is. It is a specific type of ultrasound performed during early pregnancy between 11 to 13 weeks of gestation. The purpose of this scan is to measure the fluid-filled space present at the back of the fetus's neck. The amount of fluid present is known as the nuchal translucency measurement. The measurement is used as a screening tool for chromosomal abnormalities such as Down syndrome, Edward syndrome, and Patau syndrome.

In your case, the NT measurement is 2.2 mm, which falls under the normal range. Usually, a measurement of less than 3.5mm is considered normal. So, there is no cause for concern regarding the nuchal translucency measurement.

The nasal bone is also a part of the NT scan, and a visible nasal bone is considered as an important marker for normal fetal development. In your report, it is mentioned that nasal bone could not be discretely seen. However, it is essential to understand that nasal bone visualization could be challenging during early pregnancy, and this does not necessarily indicate any abnormality. This feature is measured along with other screening tests for a thorough evaluation.

Coming to the double marker blood test, it is a specific blood test that measures the levels of two hormones, namely pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) and free beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (free β-hCG). answer_chatgpt:
Certainly! I would be happy to help differentiate these conditions.

Scabies is a parasitic infestation caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei. It typically presents with intense itching, especially at night, and a rash consisting of small red bumps and blisters. The rash may appear in the webbing between the fingers, wrists, elbows, waist, buttocks, and genitals. The mite can be visualized on skin scraping under the microscope. Treatment involves topical or oral medications aimed at killing the mites.

Flea bites typically present with a cluster of small red, itchy bumps. The bites are usually found on the feet and ankles but can appear anywhere on the body. The bites can become more swollen and itchy as an allergic reaction to the flea saliva. Fleas can be seen on the skin or hair coat of pets but often require thorough examination to detect. Prevention involves flea control in pets and their environment. Treatment consists of antihistamines and hydrocortisone cream, but if the bites become infected, antibiotics may be necessary.

Bed bugs also produce red, itchy welts that can appear in a clustering pattern. They are often found on exposed skin such as arms, face, or neck. Bed bugs, unlike fleas, cannot jump and are mainly transported on baggage, luggage or clothing. Examination of the bedding, furniture, and clothes can sometimes reveal evidence of bed bugs such as blood spots, shed skins, or bed bug excrement. Treatment includes the use of insecticides and vacuuming of affected areas.

Folliculitis is inflammation and infection of the hair follicles. It may appear as red or white bumps, pus-filled blisters, or scabs. It can be caused by Staphylococcus aureus bacteria or other organisms such as fungi or viruses. Folliculitis can occur anywhere on the body where hair follicles are present, but it is most commonly seen on the scalp, face, groin, buttocks and legs. Treatment includes topical antibiotics, antifungal or antiviral medications depending on the underlying cause.

I hope this helps!

answer_chatgpt:
Diastolic dysfunction is a condition where the heart has trouble filling with blood during the relaxation phase between heartbeats. The measurements you mentioned are related to the velocity of blood flow during this phase.

Velocity E refers to the early diastolic filling velocity. In a healthy heart, this velocity is usually between 60-80 cm/s. Your velocity E of 84.2 cm/s suggests that the initial filling of blood into your heart is slightly higher than normal.

MVA (mitral valve area) max velocity refers to the speed of blood flow through the mitral valve, which is the valve between the left atrium and left ventricle of the heart. A higher velocity through the mitral valve can indicate that the valve is not opening properly, causing an obstruction in blood flow.

In your case, your MVA max velocity of 133.5 cm/s is within the normal range, indicating that there is no significant obstruction in the mitral valve.

It is important to note that diastolic dysfunction is a complex condition and these measurements can only provide a partial evaluation. Your doctor will need to consider other factors such as your symptoms, medical history, and additional diagnostic tests to determine the proper course of treatment for you.

input: Hello doctor,What is meant by 6/6 right eye, 6/6 left eye and 6/5 uniocular vision with glasses?
answer_icliniq: Hi. In laymen terms, 6 by 6 means scientificly defined perfect vision. In medical terms, 6 by 6 means what you see from six meters, a person with normal vision also sees it from 6 metres. 6 by 5 means what a normal person sees from 5 metres you see it from 6 metres only means better than normal vision. In this case, 6 by 5 is possible with spectacles.
answer_chatgpt:
"6/6" is a measure of visual acuity, also known as "20/20" in the United States. It means that a person can see objects at a distance of 6 meters (20 feet) that a person with normal vision can also see at the same distance. 

"Right eye 6/6, left eye 6/6" means that each eye individually has normal visual acuity without the need for correction with glasses. 

"Unocular vision with glasses 6/5" means that when the person wears glasses, they can see objects at a distance of 6 meters that a person with normal vision can see at 5 meters (16.5 feet). This means their vision with glasses is better than average.
answer_chatdoctor: 6/6 means perfect 20/20 vision. 6/6 both eyes together or 6/6 right eye and 6/6 left eye mean that there is no problem in either eye when tested separately. 6/5 uniocular vision with glasses means that one eye (right or left) has better than 20/20 vision while other eye needs glasses to see clearly. This means that if you wear glasses for reading, your distance vision will be blurred without them.

A CT scan of the abdomen is a specialized imaging study that can evaluate many different organs in the abdomen including the adrenal glands, liver, pancreas, kidneys, and gallbladder among others. answer_icliniq: Hello, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. The fact that dengue cannot happen in the same season is true to some extent but not absolutely. Let me explain. Dengue is a viral infection caused by the bite of infected ades aegypti mosquito. Every mosquito bite will not lead to dengue fever as for infection to happen. First, the mosquito should be infected by the dengue virus (DEV). By infection of the mosquito I mean, the mosquito just serves as a vector or carrier for virus transfer to humans. Also, every mosquito carrying the dengue virus would not lead to dengue fever, shock, etc. Some people just have subclinical, asymptomatic infections too. There are actually four types of dengue viruses numbered from 1 to 4. Infection with one type, followed by recovery confers immunity to that type of infection. Our body produces antibodies against the virus and protects us from further infection, with time these antibodies fade away. So immunity in DEV is present but is short-lived. It can be said that the infection cannot occur in the same season, but if an infection with another type say (DEV type 1 followed by DEV type 2) occurs, the body does not have antibodies which are protective against type 2, as the body was previously infected by DEV type 1. This type of infection is more dangerous. However, in a season only one type of DEV infection occurs usually. I hope this helps.
